entities.summary: Shamanism: A 72,000-year-old practice that involves practitioners entering altered states of consciousness to interact with a spirit world. This ancient practice has been a vital part of many global cultures, influencing spiritual beliefs and rituals. Shamanic practices have been observed in various forms across the world, from the indigenous peoples of North America to the Siberian Tatars. The earliest evidence of shamanic practices dates back to the Upper Paleolithic period, with cave paintings and artifacts found in modern-day Siberia and Mongolia revealing the presence of shamanic rituals. Shamanism has played a significant role in shaping the spiritual and cultural identity of many societies, and its influence can still be seen in modern spiritual and therapeutic practices. The practice has been passed down through generations, with each culture adapting and evolving it to suit their unique beliefs and practices. Despite its ancient roots, shamanism remains a vibrant and dynamic force, continuing to inspire and captivate people around the world. In the 19th century, the Russian explorer Nikolai Przibyshev documented the shamanic practices of the Evenks people in Siberia, providing valuable insights into the spiritual worldviews of these indigenous peoples. The discovery of shamanic artifacts and texts in the 20th century has shed new light on the history and spread of shamanism, revealing its connections to other spiritual traditions and its role in shaping the course of human history. Shamanism has also had a profound impact on the development of modern psychology, with the work of Carl Jung drawing heavily on shamanic concepts and practices. The practice has also influenced the development of modern spiritual movements, such as Wicca and Neo-Shamanism, which have drawn on shamanic traditions and symbolism. In recent years, shamanism has experienced a resurgence of interest, with many people seeking out shamanic practices and rituals as a way to connect with nature and promote personal growth and healing. Despite its many benefits, shamanism has also been the subject of controversy and criticism, with some viewing it as a form of pseudoscience or a threat to mainstream spirituality. Nevertheless, shamanism remains a vital and dynamic force, continuing to inspire and captivate people around the world.
